The module_designation field: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since the cert covers multiple configurations, I could set module_designation to "Analog load cell" for the analog config... Actually the cert covers two configurations. Perhaps I should use config_level characteristics for these two configurations. The schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Hmm. The certified type is an indicator, which per R76 typically doesn't have a module designation... but the characteristics table lists "Configuration: Analog load cells". I'll set module_designation to null and handle configurations via config_level.

Role: type_evaluation_report seems apt since OIML test reports are type evaluation reports. I'll use "test_report" for these. Actually the schema says role: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. These are test reports associated with the certificate. I'll use "test_report".

- Maximum load cell resistance: 3300 Ω

Configurations as components? The schema has components[] with role, type_designations, alternatives, characteristics. The indicator cert covers two configurations. I could record the configurations in config_level. Let me use config_level entries with axis "configuration":

config_level entries:
1. attribute: "accuracy_class", axis: "configuration", values: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: "III or IIII"}, {condition: "Digital load cells or weighing module", value: "Matching the accuracy class of the digital load cell or weighing module"}]

But the values in config_level should follow structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Rules say values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So value can be string.

Actually, maybe I should organize the characteristics differently. The schema's characteristics.type_level is "whole-cert attributes — single value". Things like temperature range, environment classes, power supply apply to all configs → type_level.

Config-specific attributes → config_level with axis "configuration" or "overvoltage_protection".

type_level:
- temperature_range: {value: {min:-10, max:40}, unit_symbol: "°C"}
- mechanical_environment_class: "M3"
- electromagnetic_environment_class: "E3"

config_level entries with axis "configuration":

config_level:
1. {attribute: "accuracy_class", axis: "configuration", values: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: "III or IIII"}, {condition: "Digital load cell or weighing module", value: "Matching the accuracy class of the digital load cell or weighing module"}]}

The rule says "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". So value inside can itself be a range object {min, max}. I'll do: {"condition": "without overvoltage protection", "value": {"max": 10000}}. Hmm, value must be number|string|{min,max}. So {"value": {"min": null, "max": 10000}} is fine.

Actually simpler: value: "≤ 10000"? No — numbers preferred. Use {min: null, max: 10000}.

3. {attribute: "maximum_number_of_partial_weighing_ranges", axis: "configuration", values: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: 3}, {condition: "Digital load cell or weighing module", value: 3}]} — same for both; could be type_level "maximum_number_of_weighing_ranges": 3. I'll put at config_level to be faithful, or type_level as max_partial_weighing_ranges: 3. Both are 3, so type_level is fine. Hmm, but I want to be faithful. I'll put type_level: maximum_number_of_partial_weighing_ranges: 3.

Rule says numbers preferred. I'll add separate attribute load_cell_excitation_waveform: "square wave". Actually maybe keep it simpler: value 5, unit "V", and add attribute "load_cell_excitation_waveform": "square wave".

6. minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: 0.2 µV (analog) — config_level

Canonical label: "fraction_of_maximum_permittable_error" → "fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error". config_level with two conditions.
10. load_cell_interface: analog only — config_level, value string "6-wire with sense technology, may be configured as 4-wire"
11. maximum_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section: axis "overvoltage_protection and sense technology"... Values: without OVP: 2712.4 m/mm²; with OVP: 2909.3 m/mm² with sense technology. axis: "overvoltage_protection". values: [{condition: "without overvoltage protection", value: 2712.4, unit_symbol: "m/mm²"}, {condition: "with overvoltage protection, with sense technology", value: 2909.3, unit_symbol: "m/mm²"}]

I'll add "load_cell_power_supply_type": "DC". Or keep as string "12 V DC". Hmm. I'll do structured: value 12, unit_symbol "V", and attribute label includes dc: "load_cell_power_supply_dc"? Simpler: attribute "load_cell_power_supply_voltage", value 12, unit "V"; add note in another attribute? I'll include "load_cell_power_supply_type": "DC". Fine.

Also maximum_number_of_scale_intervals for digital config: "Equal to the maximum number of scale intervals of the digital load cell or weighing module" → config_level value string.
